scene_description: Both images show a small pale room with a light blue three-seat sofa against the back wall, a right-side chaise or ottoman, a foreground coffee table on a round rug, left-wall artwork and low console, and a tall open shelving unit at right. A narrow white cabinet, floor lamp, and framed reflective-looking rectangle occupy the back wall area.

visible_objects.observations: The principal furniture and wall decorations are represented in the candidate. The reference sofa has thick rounded cushions and arms; the candidate's are more boxy. Both show a low white console, floor lamp, white cabinet, open wooden shelves, patterned coffee table, round rug, artwork and a framed wall rectangle.
visible_objects.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, full images; sofa approximately reference [0.24,0.26,0.66,0.66], candidate [0.34,0.38,0.61,0.62].

spatial_relations_and_orientation.observations: The candidate preserves the sofa along the back wall, chaise on its right, table in front, low console to the left, and shelving to the right. Its floor lamp and cabinet are also to the sofa's right. The increased visible room width and more distant composition make the furniture appear less tightly packed than in the reference.
spatial_relations_and_orientation.image_evidence: Reference full image versus candidate full image; reference right shelving [0.70,0.00,1.00,1.00], candidate [0.68,0.13,0.99,0.93].

proportions_and_occlusion.observations: The reference sofa and foreground shelves occupy much more of the frame; the reference table and left console are cut off at the bottom, while the candidate table, shelf and much of the console fit in frame. The candidate chaise is narrower and more integrated into the sofa outline. The candidate artwork is fully visible, whereas the reference artwork extends beyond the frame.
proportions_and_occlusion.image_evidence: Reference table [0.38,0.66,0.67,1.00] versus candidate [0.39,0.61,0.61,0.92]; reference artwork [0.00,0.00,0.22,0.53] versus candidate [0.15,0.14,0.26,0.51].

materials_and_texture.observations: The reference has warm, visibly grained wooden shelves, lavender-textured walls, a pale pink rug and a brown reflective striped tabletop. The candidate shelves are flatter pale beige, the walls and rug are more neutral, and the tabletop stripes are much finer and denser, with a conspicuous dark wedge at its left edge. The reference artwork has a saturated dark blue field and a larger pink-and-yellow landform; the candidate field is paler and its shape smaller and simplified.

visible_geometry.observations: Both sofas have three separate back and seat cushions, but the candidate cushions are more rectangular with pronounced gaps and a thinner-looking base. The reference right shelving shows deep, broad cubbies with thick wood surfaces; the candidate shows a more regular grid with visible dark marks at several joints. The candidate table legs are visible, while the reference table is cropped before its legs can be assessed.

camera_and_composition.observations: The reference is a closer, more downward-looking and strongly cropped view, with the right shelf dominating the foreground and the sofa spanning much of the image width. The candidate is a wider, more centered room view, reveals the ceiling and more floor, and presents the back wall and furnishings at smaller scale.
camera_and_composition.image_evidence: Reference and candidate full images; ceiling is visible across the top of the candidate but not the reference.

lighting_and_shadows.observations: Both scenes are brightly and softly lit with subdued shadows. The reference is warmer and somewhat more colorful, especially on the wood and lavender wall; the candidate is flatter, paler and more gray-white overall. The candidate has soft floor shadows beneath the table and near furniture.
lighting_and_shadows.image_evidence: Reference and candidate full images, particularly the right shelving and floor beneath the table.

objects_regions.observation: Large rounded pale blue three-seat sofa with right-hand projecting cushion; candidate is smaller in frame with more squared cushions and a narrower projection.
Warm wood-grained shelving fills the right foreground and is heavily cropped; candidate is fully framed, paler and more uniform, with dark joint marks.
The reference tabletop is brown and reflective with broad diagonal streaks; candidate has finer light stripes and a black wedge at the left edge, and its legs are visible.
The saturated dark blue artwork is substantially cropped in the reference; candidate shows a smaller complete frame with a paler field and simplified shape.
Low white open console sits to the left of the table in both; it is much more cropped and larger in the reference.
Reference frame is cropped at top and shows a faint reflection; candidate frame is smaller, fully visible and more uniformly pale.
Both are at the right end of the sofa. Their general placement is retained, although they occupy a smaller portion of the candidate frame.
The reference rug appears pale pink and is substantially cropped; the candidate rug is nearly white and its circular outline is more visible.

most_important_visible_defects: The camera framing is markedly wider and less close than the reference, changing the apparent scale and cropping of nearly every object.
The right shelving loses much of the reference's warm wood grain and dominant foreground presence.
The coffee table's finer stripe pattern and dark wedge differ noticeably from the broad reflective reference streaks.
Sofa cushions are more boxy and the chaise appears less substantial; the artwork's color and framing also differ.
uncertainty: The back-wall rectangle may be a mirror or a framed image; its precise function is not established. Apparent size differences can result from camera placement or field of view rather than actual object dimensions. Exact contact, hidden surfaces, physical scale and symmetry cannot be established from these images alone.
limitations: Evaluation is based only on the two supplied RGB images, using approximate normalized image coordinates. Bright exposure and occlusion limit assessment of fine material properties, geometry and shadows. No unseen surfaces or underlying implementation were evaluated.
